title: a second chance at the life i always wanted

body.text: for a long time, i had my hands on the life i wanted. i had the vision, the ambition + the opportunity to build something meaningful for myself. but somewhere along the way, my immaturity showed. my lack of focus showed. i made decisions that pulled me away from the very things i said i wanted.
and eventually, i had to live with the consequences.

that's one of the harder things about growing up ~ realizing that some of the things you're frustrated with today are the results of choices you made yesterday. you can look back and recognize where you went wrong, where you lost focus, and where you allowed temporary distractions to take you off course.
but at some point, reflection has to become responsibility.
i cannot keep being upset about a life that looks different because of decisions i made. i have to accept where i am, own how i got here + build from that reality.
lately, i've been thinking about second chances.
not a second chance to repeat the same mistakes. not another opportunity to take something for granted. but a chance to demonstrate that the lessons from the first time actually meant something.
a chance to prove that i've grown into someone who can appreciate, maintain + build upon the opportunities i once had.

because the truth is, the life i wanted wasn't necessarily missing. in many ways, it was right there in front of me. i just wasn't always mature enough, disciplined enough, or focused enough to choose it consistently.
now, i'm choosing differently.

at 30, i'm learning to humble my ego, move with more intention + take the lessons from my early 20s into this next chapter. i'm learning that maturity isn't just knowing what you should have done. it's having the discipline to do what you know needs to be done now.
and that means accepting that things aren't exactly how they used to be.
i can't keep measuring my present against a past that no longer exists. i can't spend all my energy thinking about what could have been while neglecting what can still become.
i have to work with what i have, where i am, and make better decisions moving forward.
a new job. a new opportunity. a new chapter of my life.
i'm grateful for the opportunity to get back on the path i always wanted to be on. and this time, i want to approach it with a different level of appreciation, discipline + understanding.
because a second chance means very little if you bring the same version of yourself into it.
i don't need to prove that my past was perfect. i need to prove that i've learned from it.
i don't need to pretend that i made all the right decisions. i need to take responsibility for the ones i didn't.
and i don't need to spend the rest of my life looking backward, wishing i had chosen differently.
i can choose differently now.
from this moment forward, my focus is on moving forward ~ becoming wiser, building with intention, honoring the opportunities in front of me + creating a life that reflects the man i'm becoming.
i'm not starting from zero. i'm starting from experience.
and for that, i'm grateful.
